title: Directed interval enclosure for the fixed rounded residual snapshot
question: Can directed interval arithmetic certify the residual minimum eigenvalue and both fixed-reference separations for the exact IEEE-754 rounded R-428/R-429 graph snapshot at the R-426 failure row?

new_perspective.principle: Replace the downstream point eigensolve by a finite interval certificate: treat each stored binary64 snapshot value as an exact binary rational, propagate directed intervals through the weighted residual basis and compression, certify a lower bound by interval Cholesky, and certify an upper bound by an interval Rayleigh quotient.
route: Reconstruct the fixed R-426 row through the existing R-429 snapshot producer without importing the R-431 primary result.
Convert every binary64 weight and conductance to its exact binary rational interval and use 80-digit directed mpmath interval arithmetic for square roots, products and divisions.

Construct the blockwise weighted-zero-mean residual basis by interval Gram-Schmidt, symmetrise by interval hull, and prove A-LI positive definite by an interval Cholesky factorization at the declared lower probe.
Use an independent floating-point Rayleigh vector with an interval quotient for the upper probe; compare the certified bracket with R-422 and R-426 under the unchanged 5e-7 tolerance.
Keep the original Hamiltonian/Gibbs source enclosure explicitly outside scope; the result is a rigorous finite certificate only for the fixed rounded snapshot.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: The certificate removes downstream eigensolver ambiguity for one rounded finite graph row, but it supplies no original-source enclosure, common core, regulator limit, physical sector or Yang-Mills statement.

interval_contract.input_mode: exact binary64 snapshot values reconstructed as binary rationals

assumptions: The R-429 row_inputs producer and its hash-pinned upstream manifests define the exact finite rounded snapshot under audit.
A stored binary64 value is treated as its exact binary rational; no unrecorded decimal rounding is introduced.
Directed interval operations enclose the finite arithmetic expressions used for the residual matrix and basis.
Interval Cholesky positivity of A-LI proves the lower eigenvalue bound, and an interval Rayleigh quotient proves an upper bound for the same symmetric matrix.
The blockwise weighted-zero-mean basis and fixed row/tail split are unchanged from R-426/R-429.
missing_assumptions: A validated interval eigensolve for the original 256-dimensional Hamiltonian and coordinate eigenbasis.
A propagated enclosure from the original rational source through Gibbs normalization, conditional-row selection and conductance.
A basis-independent certified residual comparison for the unrounded original source.
A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform common Q3 core and OS/KMS/GNS/physical-sector transfer.
stop_conditions: If the interval basis loses positivity, orthogonality or finite width, report the rounded snapshot certificate as blocked and do not relax the probes.
If either reference separation fails at the fixed tolerance, retain the exact interval bracket and do not convert it into a source-level conclusion.
Never mark the original-source residual-reuse route closed from this downstream snapshot certificate.
evidence_level: T0 / EXECUTED RIGOROUS FINITE INTERVAL CERTIFICATE FOR ONE EXACT BINARY64 ROUNDED GRAPH SNAPSHOT; original Hamiltonian source enclosure remains open
non_claims: No interval certification of the original Hamiltonian, coordinate eigenbasis or Gibbs weights.
No closure of R-426 residual reuse for the original unrounded source.
No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform Schur or residual bound.
No common core, history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, sector gap or continuum limit.
No C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
boundary: R-431 certifies a narrow eigenvalue bracket and fixed-reference separations for the exact rounded R-428/R-429 graph snapshot. It does not enclose the upstream Hamiltonian/Gibbs construction, so the original-source precision boundary and R-426 route status remain separate.
next_unlock: Build a validated interval or ball enclosure for the original coordinate and Hamiltonian eigensystems, then propagate it through Gibbs normalization and residual compression at the same fixed row.

lean_crosscheck.role: Lean checks the rational threshold arithmetic and explicit finite/no-source-promotion scope; interval matrix operations remain executable Python.
